LocusMimic is intended only for lawful testing, development, device debugging, and personal learning. Do not use it to bypass platform rules, commit fraud, invade privacy, or perform any illegal activity. Map display, place search, and reverse geocoding are provided by Baidu Map JavaScript API, which is loaded only after you consent. You are responsible for how this tool is used.
I agree to lawful testing use and to loading Baidu Map JavaScript API for map features.

Suppresses the toast shown when the module activates in a target app

Off (default): blocks the BroadcastReceiver — no app or ADB shell can start/stop spoofing or set coordinates via intents. On: any installed app and \'adb shell am broadcast\' can drive the module (no permission check; coordinates are clamped to valid lat/lon ranges). Only enable this if you trust every app on the device or are running on a controlled (e.g., automation) device. See docs/EXTERNAL_CONTROL.md for actions and lock-down options.
Requires Root and LSPosed. Only affects apps selected in the app list. Suitable for most apps, with extremely low resource and battery usage.

Requires Root and LSPosed. In addition to app-level hooks, it handles Android system, framework, and phone services. It is intended for apps with unusual location paths or stronger mock-location detection. Compatibility is better, but system location issues may occur on a small number of devices. Resource and battery usage remain extremely low.

Does not require Root or LSPosed, but you must first select LocusMimic under Developer options → Select mock location app. Android marks the location as mocked, so target apps may detect it. The LocusMimic background service must remain running during simulation, with relatively higher resource and battery usage.
